# **FG-03 \-- 012 \-- Browse Product Catalog**

1. # **Use-Case Name**

   UC-012 — Browse Product Catalog

   1. ## **Brief Description**

   A Guest or Customer explores published electronic products through the storefront homepage, category navigation, and product catalog listings. The System presents category and product summaries so the actor can discover products before opening an individual product page.

   Functional group: FG-03 — Search and Browse

   Actor(s): Guest (G), Customer (C)

   Priority: Core

2. # **Flow of Events**

   1. ## **Basic Flow**

   1\. The Guest or Customer opens the storefront homepage.

   2\. The System displays storefront navigation, product categories, and homepage product sections that provide entry points to the catalog. The selection and ranking of homepage recommendations are covered separately by UC-019 View Homepage Recommendations.

   3\. The Guest or Customer selects a category from the homepage/category navigation or opens the all-products catalog.

   4\. The System retrieves the published products for the selected category, or the full published catalog when the all-products view is requested.

   5\. The System displays the category listing, including the category name, product count, product cards, and pagination controls when the result spans multiple pages.

   6\. The System presents the product summary fields available in the listing, such as product name, image, price, discount, and selected technical attributes; ratings or availability are displayed where the catalog data and design provide them.

   7\. The Guest or Customer browses the product cards and may move between available listing pages.

   8\. The Guest or Customer may select a product to continue with UC-015 View Product Details, or use the separate search, filter, sort, and comparison functions covered by UC-013, UC-014, and UC-016.

   2. ## **Alternative Flows**

      1. ### *Input validation and business-rule alternatives*

   A1. The selected category is unknown, removed, or no longer published: the System displays an unavailable-category state and provides a route back to the catalog or homepage. No unpublished category or product data is exposed.

   A2. The selected category contains no published products: the System displays an empty-category state and provides a route to browse other categories or all products. This state is a required behavior but is not represented by a dedicated empty-category screen in the Hza.zip export.

   A3. The catalog contains no published products: the System displays an explanatory empty-catalog state instead of a blank page or fabricated product cards. The Hza.zip export does not contain a dedicated empty-catalog screen.

      2. ### *Additional outcomes and service failures*

   A4. The catalog request fails or times out: the System displays a recoverable error state and a retry action. It must not present fabricated product records or label stale data as current. A customer-facing catalog error screen is not present in the Hza.zip export.

   A5. A product becomes unavailable or unpublished after the listing is loaded: the System must not expose the unavailable product as purchasable. If the Guest or Customer opens the affected item, UC-015 View Product Details handles the unavailable-product outcome.

3. # **Special Requirements**

   1. ## **Use-case quality and integrity constraints**

   • Catalog browsing is available to both Guests and Customers; authentication is not required to view public categories and product listings.

   • Only products published for storefront display may appear in the public catalog. The exact visibility rule for inactive, discontinued, or out-of-stock variants must be confirmed with Backend.

   • Product names, images, prices, discounts, specifications, ratings, and availability must come from authoritative catalog data. The UI must not invent missing values.

   • Prices must be displayed in VND with consistent formatting. Pagination must clearly indicate the current page and the available result range.

   • The storefront should remain usable on supported desktop and mobile layouts. Hza.zip includes desktop and mobile catalog screen exports; these static exports do not establish responsive behavior across all viewport sizes.

   • Product examples, prices, discounts, and counts shown in the Hza.zip PDF exports are sample content and are not evidence of live or implemented catalog data.

4. # **Preconditions**

   1. ## **Conditions that must hold**

   • The storefront is reachable.

   • The catalog service and category data are available, or the System can return a defined empty/error state.

   • The Guest or Customer can access the public storefront. No authenticated session is required for this use case.

5. # **Postconditions**

   1. ## **Success and failure states**

   Success:

   • The requested homepage or category product listing is displayed.

   • The Guest or Customer can continue to a related search, filter, comparison, or product-detail use case.

   • No catalog or product data is modified by browsing.

   Failure:

   • No unpublished or unauthorized catalog data is exposed.

   • No fabricated product, price, discount, rating, or availability information is displayed.

   • No persistent business data is changed.

6. # **Extension Points**

   1. ## **Related use cases and scope**

   No formal UML extension point is defined in the current shared use-case model. Related use cases:

   • UC-013 — Search Products

   • UC-014 — Filter & Sort Products

   • UC-015 — View Product Details

   • UC-016 — Compare Products

   • UC-017 — View Product Promotions

   • UC-019 — View Homepage Recommendations

   • UC-022 — Manage Wishlist

   Scope: This specification is based on Vision v1.4, the shared Use-Case Model, and the static screen exports in Hza.zip. The desktop category PDF shows a category listing with one active RAM filter; applying or removing filters and changing sort order belong to UC-014 Filter & Sort Products, not the default browse flow. The mobile product-list PDF has the search field prefilled with “iPhone” and a Filter & Sort control; searching and filtering belong to UC-013 Search Products and UC-014 Filter & Sort Products. These frames are used only to evidence catalog/listing presentation and responsive layout. The homepage PDF includes category entry points and featured products; recommendation selection and ranking belong to UC-019 View Homepage Recommendations. Hza.zip contains static PDF exports, not interactive prototype data, so clickable transitions and prototype reactions cannot be verified from the supplied files. The screens contain sample content and do not prove implementation or testing.

   Performed by: Nguyễn Hoàng Gia \| Reviewed by: Pending \| Status: Draft for review
